To find the stationary points of a function y = f(x), first, find the first derivative of the function, f'(x). Then, set the first derivative equal to zero and solve for x. These solutions are the x-coordinates of the stationary points. To determine the nature of each stationary point, find the second derivative, f''(x), and evaluate it at each x-coordinate. If f''(x) > 0, the point is a local minimum. If f''(x) < 0, the point is a local maximum. If f''(x) = 0, the test is inconclusive.
